Diego/Tom/Sara — attaching a draft with tracked changes. Summary of recommended edits:
1) Exhibit E: change retention for non-production logs from 30 days to 7 days (we recommend adding a short definition for "non-production logs" to avoid scope creep).
2) Change-of-control: BrightHarbor asked earlier about change-of-control protections — we propose adding limited termination rights tied to a >50% ownership change, with a 60-day cure.
3) Tier rebalance language: added a new Schedule 2 section that describes a 90-day burst window (up to 40% of committed units), a stepped ramp-down schedule, and the corresponding effective per-unit uplift for the bursted capacity. Pricing table in the order form shows both baseline and bursted unit prices.
4) Term: BrightHarbor indicated preference for an 18-month term for price stability — updated the Order Form to reflect 18 months with pro-rated month 1.

I flag two commercial negotiation points for your attention (Ben/Diego):
- We included an explicit cap that the burst window cannot be combined with a separate overage credit for the same billing period (to avoid double-crediting).
- We added a short audit clause to record usage reconciliation within 45 days of each quarter.

Attachments: MSA_changes_markup_20270811.docx, BrightHarbor_proposed_orderform_v2.pdf

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks for the quick markup, this mostly looks great. A couple of follow-ups from legal/procurement:
- Can we soften the change-of-control termination right to allow assignment to an affiliate without triggering termination? (They want to avoid blocking strategic M&A that keeps control in the same group.)
- On retention, happy with 7 days for non-prod logs provided the definition is explicit.
- Pricing: procurement would like the burst uplift to be capped at a 15% premium over baseline (your markup goes slightly higher). Would you accept a cap at 15% for the first 3 months, then a review?

If we can land those items, Sara can shepherd the DocuSign signature. I can sign on BrightHarbor’s side quickly.

Best,
Tom
